topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's focus on the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen Recognition and PRR Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses pathogens and cellular damage through molecular patterns, pattern recognition receptors, and downstream signaling complexes such as the inflammasome.

topics.label: Inflammatory Cell Activation, Trafficking, and Systemic Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how activated sentinel cells orchestrate leukocyte recruitment into tissues, transport antigens via lymphatics, and can trigger severe systemic outcomes like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, drive tissue healing, or lead to chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the complement system.
